Synthesis of Transition Metal-Chalcogenide NPs as Anode Material for LIB and Related Applications

Abstract:

Transition-metal chalcogenides (TMCs) have attracted considerable attention as multifunctional nanomaterials because of their tuneable electronic structures, high electrical conductivity, and excellent catalytic activity. This research focuses on the design and synthesis of iron-based chalcogenide nanoparticles using stable single-source molecular precursors, enabling precise control over composition, crystallinity, and morphology. The synthesized nanomaterials will be systematically characterized and further modified with carbon-based materials, including graphene derivatives and carbon quantum dots, to enhance their electrochemical performance. Particular emphasis is placed on FeSe2 as a high-capacity anode material for lithium-ion batteries, where its high theoretical capacity and improved conductivity offer enhanced lithium storage and cycling stability. In addition, the materials will be investigated for electrocatalytic hydrogen and oxygen evolution reactions, and photocatalysis. This work provides a facile and scalable strategy for developing cost-effective, high-performance chalcogenide nanomaterials for sustainable energy storage and conversion.
